The problem
Australia has no way for pet owners to
find
clinical trials.
In the United States, the AVMA Veterinary Clinical Trials Registry, AniTrial, and the Dog Aging Project connect pet owners with hundreds of active studies. Dog and cat owners there can access new cancer immunotherapy, longevity drugs like rapamycin, and novel treatments for kidney disease, epilepsy, and arthritis.
In Australia, clinical research is fragmented across seven veterinary schools with no centralised, owner-accessible registry. Pet owners have no way to discover if a trial relevant to their pet's condition exists. They cannot enrol. Research teams struggle to recruit participants.
PetTrials fixes that. For free.
No centralised trial registry
Unlike the US, which has the AVMA registry with hundreds of active studies, Australian pet owners have nowhere to search for trials.
Research fragmented across 7 vet schools
UQ, Sydney, Melbourne, Murdoch, CSU, JCU, and Adelaide each run independent studies with no shared recruitment platform.
Researchers cannot find participants
Veterinary clinical trials depend on owner participation. Without a matching platform, recruitment is slow and studies are underpowered.
Pets miss out on life-saving treatments
Pets with cancer, chronic disease, or age-related conditions could benefit from new therapies, but only if their owners knew the trials existed.
How it works
Three steps to
better
care for your pet.
Upload your pet's health records, get matched with relevant studies, and connect directly with research teams. Everything is free for pet owners.
Step 01
Upload
Upload your dog or cat's vaccination records, diagnoses, medications, surgical history, and vet visit notes. Build a complete longitudinal health profile that grows with your pet. Completely free.
Step 02
Match
Our matching engine compares your pet's profile against active clinical trials at Australian universities and research institutions. When a relevant study opens, you are notified immediately.
Step 03
Connect
Review study details, eligibility, and what participation involves. PetTrials arranges introductions with research teams and guides you through informed consent and enrolment.
Research areas
Active and emerging trial
areas

Australian veterinary schools run research across a growing range of conditions. These are the therapeutic areas where trials are most active or expected to recruit.
Cancer
Osteosarcoma, lymphoma, mast cell tumours, hemangiosarcoma, immunotherapy, CAR-T.
Heart disease
Cardiomyopathy, valve disease, rapamycin studies, heart failure management.
Kidney disease
Chronic kidney disease, novel therapeutics, dietary interventions.
Neurology
Epilepsy, degenerative myelopathy, cognitive decline, seizure management.
Gastrointestinal
Chronic enteropathy, inflammatory bowel disease, microbiome therapies.
Orthopaedics
Osteoarthritis, joint disease, pain management, regenerative medicine.
Dermatology
Atopic dermatitis, pyoderma, novel topical therapies, allergy management.
Ageing & longevity
Rapamycin, lifespan extension, age-related disease prevention, biological ageing.

For pet owners
Your pet's health history, in
one
place.
Even if there is no trial available for your pet right now, PetTrials gives you something no other Australian platform offers: a centralised, secure digital health record for your dog or cat.
Upload vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, and surgical history. Track changes over time. Share your profile with any vet. And when a trial does open that matches your pet's condition, you will be the first to know.
Think of it as a health passport for your pet, built for the future of veterinary medicine.

For researchers

Veterinary clinical trials depend on finding the right animals with the right conditions. PetTrials gives research teams access to a growing database of pet health profiles, pre-screened and ready for eligibility matching.
List your trial on PetTrials for free. Reach pet owners who are actively looking for research opportunities. Reduce recruitment timelines and improve enrolment rates.
List your trial
Pre-screened profiles
Owners upload detailed vet histories including diagnoses, medications, and procedures, enabling rapid eligibility assessment.
Targeted recruitment
When you list a trial, PetTrials notifies owners whose pets match your inclusion criteria. No more passive waiting for referrals.
Recruitment analytics
Track views, enquiries, and enrolment rates for your listed studies through the PetTrials research dashboard.
Free to list
Listing trials on PetTrials is free for Australian veterinary schools and research institutions. Always.

FAQ
Common
questions
.
Is PetTrials really free for pet owners?
+
Yes. Uploading your pet's vet history, receiving trial match notifications, and connecting with research teams costs nothing. PetTrials is funded by Altered Carbon Synthetic Biology and by research partnerships.
What information do I need to upload?
+
As much as you have: vaccination records, diagnoses, medications, surgical history, vet visit notes. The more complete your profile, the better we can match you with relevant trials.
Is it safe to join a clinical trial?
+
All veterinary clinical trials at Australian institutions are reviewed by Animal Ethics Committees (AECs) under the Australian Code for the Care and Use of Animals for Scientific Purposes. Your pet's welfare is the top priority.
Can I withdraw my pet from a trial?
+
Absolutely. Participation is always voluntary and you can withdraw at any stage. Informed consent is required before enrolment and is not a binding contract.
What if there is no trial for my pet right now?
+
Your profile stays active. When a new study opens that matches your pet's condition, breed, or age, you will be notified automatically. New trials are listed regularly.
Is this only for dogs?
+
PetTrials launched with a focus on dogs, since they represent the largest clinical trial population. Cat trials are already listed and the cat profile flow is being added as the platform grows.
What happens to my pet's data?
+
Your data is stored securely in Australia under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). It is only used for trial matching and is never shared with third parties without your explicit consent. See our
Privacy Policy
.
